title: Unified Metric Composer for Quant Calibration Sensitivity
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Summary:
We need a single, extensible scoring layer (Unified Metric Composer, UMC) to drive calibration and quality gating for FP8/INT8 quantization profiles. UMC will expose a small API to compose family-level metrics (perplexity, MMLU-style accuracy suites, Rouge/BLEU, EM/F1 for QA, and task-specific scorers) into sensitivity-aware signals used by the calibration workflow and gating orchestrator. The goal is to standardize metric computation, normalization, and aggregation so calibration runs are comparable across model variants and dataset slices.

Goals and acceptance criteria:
- Implement a modular metric interface that supports: token-level perplexity (with in-context normalization), multi-task accuracy (MMLU style, per-subject breakdown), summarization metrics (Rouge-L, Rouge-1/2, BLEU), QA EM/F1, and a plugin hook for custom task scorers.
- Provide deterministic tokenization and reference normalization rules (SentencePiece config with de-dup and punctuation normalization) to ensure reproducibility between CPU/GPU runs.
- Return: raw metric values, per-task confidence intervals (bootstrap), sensitivity curves (metric vs. quantization bit-width/scale), and an aggregated sensitivity score used by the calibration gate.
- Integrate with existing eval harness and output artifacts consumable by the calibration pipeline (CSV/Parquet + JSON manifest + prometheus-compatible metrics).

Design decisions and tradeoffs:
- Composition strategy: we will compute family-level z-scores (standardized against a baseline fp32 reference per task) and then produce a weighted linear combination for the aggregated sensitivity score. We considered rank-aggregation and geometric mean; linear combination chosen for interpretability and ease of thresholding.
- Uncertainty estimation: use bootstrap resampling (1k draws by default) at dataset-shard granularity to produce 95% CI. This is more robust to non-normal error distributions than analytic approximations.
- Perplexity definition: use cross-entropy per-token but add an in-context length normalization factor for few-shot prompts so that longer contexts don't artificially inflate perplexity. This normalization is a configurable scalar in UMC.
- BLEU/Rouge tokenization: use the platform's canonical SentencePiece tokenizer config. Detokenize references for human-readable outputs but compute metrics on tokenized forms to avoid surface-level detokenization variance.

API and data contract (high level):
- compute_metrics(run_id, model_variant, dataset_slice, metrics=["ppl","mmlu","rouge","bleu","qa_f1"], config=... ) -> writes artifacts to s3://redwood-quant-evals/{run_id}/ and returns JSON manifest string with keys: raw_csv, aggregated_score, per_task_ci, sensitivity_curve_csv.
- Metric entry format (CSV): columns = [task, input_id, prediction, reference, tokens, score].
- Manifest (JSON string returned) must be stable and include version tag for metric impl (e.g., umc-v1.0).

Implementation plan and timeline:
- Spike (2 days): prototype perplexity normalization and bootstrap CI on a small summarization + MMLU subset. (owner: Liam) - DONE: prototype notebook with results attached.
- Core impl (8 working days): metric adapters, bootstrap engine (with parallel workers), aggregation module, and CLI. (owners: ENG metrics team)
- Integration (4 working days): hook into calibration workflow: calibration-run -> compute_metrics -> calibration-gate consumes aggregated_score and CI. Add prometheus exporter for per-run metrics.
- Validation (3 working days): run full FP8/INT8 sweep on 4 models (small/medium/base/large) and produce final gating thresholds.
- Rollout (1 day): enable UMC as default metric layer for calibration job definitions, add feature flag for old metrics for 2 weeks.

Operational outputs and monitoring:
- Save artifacts to s3 with path layout: s3://redwood-quant-evals/{release}/{model}/{run_id}/umc-manifest.json and per-slice CSVs.
- Export Prometheus metrics: umc_aggregated_score{model,variant,release} and umc_metric_ci_lower/upper with run_id label.
- Console integration: add a new UMC tab under quantization profile runs showing sensitivity curves and per-task CI overlays.

Testing and gating thresholds:
- For MMLU-style tasks: require aggregated per-task delta <= 1.5% absolute from fp32 baseline OR lower CI > baseline - 2.0%.
- For perplexity: require relative PPL increase <= 8% for INT8 and <= 20% for FP8 compared to fp32 on in-context normalized metric.
- For summarization: Rouge-L relative degradation <= 3 points absolute.
- Final gating uses weighted aggregate where MMLU has weight 0.4, perplexity 0.2, summarization 0.25, QA 0.15 (configurable per release).

Security and reproducibility notes:
- Metric computations must be deterministic given the same seed and tokenizer config. Seed propagation implemented in UMC to avoid CI variance.
- No model weights or customer data are written to public buckets. All eval data are on private s3 with limited IAM roles.

Rollout risks and mitigation:
- Risk: metric normalization choices may over- or under-estimate quality. Mitigation: run A/B on a subset of customer signals and keep old gating for a minimum of 2 weeks.
- Risk: memory/CPU overhead from bootstrap resampling. Mitigation: implement streaming bootstrap with reservoir sampling and rate-limit parallelism by worker pool.

Deliverables:
- umc service + CLI (PyPI package redwood_eval_umc v1.0pre)
- Integration PRs: calibration orchestration changes and console visualization
- Confluence design doc and reproducible notebooks

Open questions (to resolve during implementation):
- Final default weights for the aggregated sensitivity score across releases (proposal in comments).
- Acceptable runtimes for bootstrap CI on large datasets (trade memory for compute).
- How to incorporate human evaluation signals (spam labeling) into composite score in a rev next sprint.
